Rarefy samples to a common depth

Source: R/rrarefy.R
el_rrarefy.Rd

Counterpart of vegan::rrarefy(): a random subsample, without replacement, of depth individuals from each sample. With no depth, the smallest sample total is used, so no sample is dropped.

Usage

el_rrarefy(
  x,
  depth = NULL,
  sample = "sample",
  taxon = "taxon",
  quant = "quant"
)

Arguments

x

A data frame or lazy duckplyr table with one row per non-zero sample and taxon, holding whole counts. Rows with quant == 0 are dropped.

depth

A single finite whole number, at least 1. The default, NULL, is the smallest total among the samples with a non-zero count.

sample, taxon, quant

Names of the columns in x. The result has only these three columns, with the same names.

Value

A duckplyr table holding the result in memory, with the samples in the order they first appear in x and without the taxa that were not drawn.

Details

A sample with a total below depth cannot be rarefied and is dropped from the result, with a warning that names it; it is an error if no sample is left. vegan returns such a sample unchanged, which leaves samples of different depths in the result. A sample whose total equals depth is kept as it is.

The result is random, so call set.seed() first for a reproducible one. It is not the same random sample as vegan's for the same seed: vegan draws the individuals one at a time, and el_rrarefy() draws the count of each taxon from the hypergeometric distribution of what is left. Both draw from the same distribution of counts (the multivariate hypergeometric).

The table is read into R and copied several times, so this is not a lazy step: allow a few times the memory of the input. Counts or totals of about 2^31 and above make each draw slow.

Examples

library(dplyr)

# A long table of read counts for 16S ASVs in a time series from the Baltic Sea.
counts <- duckplyr::read_csv_duckdb(
  system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living.tsv.gz", package = "ecolongr"),
  options = list(delim = "\t", header = TRUE), prudence = "stingy"
)
metadata <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "lmo_free_living_samples.tsv", package = "ecolongr"))

# Samples with at least 5,000 reads.
deep <- counts |>
  summarise(reads = sum(quant, na.rm = TRUE), .by = sample) |>
  filter(reads >= 5000) |>
  select(sample)
counts <- semi_join(counts, deep, by = "sample")
metadata <- filter(metadata, sample %in% as.data.frame(deep)$sample)
set.seed(1)
subsample <- el_rrarefy(counts, depth = 5000)

# Every sample now has exactly 5,000 reads, but different samples keep different ASVs.
subsample |> summarise(reads = sum(quant), .by = sample) |> head() |> as.data.frame()
#>                          sample reads
#> 1 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017  5000
#> 2 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1020  5000
#> 3 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1024  5000
#> 4 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P13006_1025  5000
#> 5 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P13006_1033  5000
#> 6 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P13006_1036  5000
el_specnumber(subsample) |> head()
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1017 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1018 
#>                           251                           236 
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1019 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1020 
#>                           222                           301 
#> LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1021 LMO_2011-2023_16S:P10353_1022 
#>                           221                           303
